COOK – FULL TIME

BUSINESS:  PAPADOPOULOS BROTHERS PTY LTD
ABN: 68 607 569 380
TRADING AS: Meli Annandale
LOCATION: 88 View Street, Annandale NSW 2038
SALARY: $79,500 – $83,000 + Superannuation (commensurate with experience)
EMPLOYMENT TYPE: Full-time (minimum 38 hours per week)

Job Published: 3 July 2026


ABOUT THE BUSINESS
Meli Annandale is a contemporary neighbourhood café located in Annandale, NSW, providing high-quality breakfast, brunch, and lunch dining within a modern hospitality environment. The café offers a diverse menu featuring freshly prepared contemporary Australian café cuisine, specialty coffee, and seasonal menu offerings, with a strong focus on quality ingredients, presentation, and customer experience.
The business operates a full-service dine-in model with prepared-to-order meals delivered across continuous daily service. Kitchen operations involve fresh ingredient preparation, coordinated food production, and efficient workflow management to meet varying customer demand, particularly during peak breakfast, brunch, and weekend trading periods.
The commercial kitchen operates under established systems and procedures, incorporating food preparation, cooking, plating, stock management, and strict compliance with Australian food safety, hygiene, and workplace health and safety standards to ensure consistent service quality and operational efficiency.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The position of Cook is a hands-on operational role responsible for preparing, cooking, and presenting menu items in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and service requirements within a contemporary café environment. The role requires the ability to manage allocated kitchen sections, maintain consistency across breakfast, brunch, and lunch service, and contribute to the efficient day-to-day operation of a commercial kitchen.
The successful candidate will work collaboratively within a team-based environment, demonstrating initiative in food preparation, coordinating workflow during service, maintaining food quality and presentation standards, and ensuring compliance with food safety and hygiene requirements.
The primary place of employment will be Meli Annandale, 88 View Street, Annandale NSW 2038. From time to time, the successful candidate may also be required to perform duties at the employer's associated hospitality venue, Sabine Bondi, Shop 505/500 Oxford Street, Bondi Junction NSW 2022, to support operational requirements. Duties performed at either location will remain consistent with the position of Cook and will be undertaken under the direction of the employer.
The role also provides ongoing opportunities for professional development through structured on-the-job training and exposure to a range of contemporary café kitchen operations and cooking techniques.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

FOOD PREPARATION AND COOKING
•	Prepare, cook, and present a range of breakfast, brunch, and lunch menu items in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and presentation requirements.
•	Undertake ingredient preparation, including washing, cutting, portioning, marinating, and pre-service mise en place to support efficient kitchen operations.
•	Apply appropriate cooking techniques including grilling, frying, roasting, baking, poaching, and sautéing while maintaining consistency in quality and presentation.
•	Follow standardised recipes and portion controls to ensure consistency, minimise wastage, and meet service expectations.
•	Adjust food preparation and cooking methods where required to accommodate service volumes, dietary requirements, and special customer requests.

SERVICE AND KITCHEN OPERATIONS
•	Support efficient kitchen workflow during breakfast, brunch, and lunch service to ensure timely preparation and delivery of meals.
•	Manage allocated kitchen sections, ensuring workstations are organised and service-ready prior to and during operational periods.
•	Communicate effectively with kitchen and front-of-house staff to support efficient service delivery and order accuracy.
•	Assist with menu execution, daily specials, and seasonal menu offerings in accordance with business requirements.
•	Adapt workflow during busy service periods while maintaining food quality, presentation, and operational efficiency.

STOCK CONTROL AND KITCHEN ORGANISATION
•	Assist in receiving, inspecting, and storing deliveries to ensure product quality and compliance with storage requirements.
•	Implement stock rotation practices, including FIFO, to maintain freshness and minimise wastage.
•	Monitor ingredient usage and report stock shortages or inconsistencies to senior kitchen staff.
•	Assist with stocktakes and maintain organised storage areas to support efficient kitchen operations.
•	Ensure appropriate labelling, storage, and handling of food products in accordance with food safety standards.

FOOD SAFETY AND COMPLIANCE
•	Maintain compliance with food safety legislation and safe food handling procedures.
•	Maintain high standards of hygiene and cleanliness across workstations, equipment, utensils, and food preparation areas.
•	Monitor storage, cooking, and holding temperatures to ensure compliance with food safety requirements.
•	Follow workplace food safety procedures, including HACCP-based practices where applicable.
•	Comply with Workplace Health and Safety requirements, including the safe operation of commercial kitchen equipment.

GENERAL DUTIES AND TEAM CONTRIBUTION
•	Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient workstation throughout each shift.
•	Follow instructions from senior kitchen staff and management with accuracy and attention to detail.
•	Work collaboratively within a team environment to support efficient kitchen operations during busy service periods.
•	Demonstrate reliability, professionalism, punctuality, and a positive approach to work.
•	Participate in ongoing training and professional development to enhance culinary skills and operational performance.

MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS
•	Relevant qualification in Commercial Cookery (Certificate III or higher) or a closely related field, or a minimum of one (1) year of relevant experience within a commercial kitchen environment.
•	Demonstrated experience preparing and cooking food within a commercial café, restaurant, or hospitality environment.
•	Sound knowledge of food safety standards, kitchen hygiene, and safe food handling practices.
•	Ability to work efficiently within a fast-paced commercial kitchen environment.
•	Availability to work weekends, public holidays, and varied rostered shifts as required.

KEY COMPETENCIES
•	Technical Cooking Proficiency
•	Contemporary Café Food Preparation
•	Recipe Interpretation & Food Presentation
•	Time Management
•	Kitchen Workflow & Operational Awareness
•	Attention to Detail
•	Communication & Team Collaboration
•	Problem Solving
•	Food Safety & Compliance
•	Commitment to Continuous Improvement

HOW TO APPLY
Please submit a one-page CV outlining your relevant experience, qualifications, and availability. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted

About Us 

Amity Care Services is a Mornington Peninsula based disability and home care support provider, founded by a team of registered nurses with extensive clinical experience in complex and acute care. We deliver Supported Independent Living, Specialist Disability Accommodation, Short Term Accommodation, Support Coordination, Psychosocial Recovery Coaching and clinical nursing services across the region, and can provide 24/7 support to our clients. Our values of loyalty, trust and honesty shape how we work with each other and the people we support. 

About the Role 

We are seeking a motivated and organised Rostering Coordinator to join our busy Rostering team at Amity Care Services. 

This role is responsible for coordinating accurate, timely and person-centred rosters for participants and support workers. You will work closely with the Rostering Lead, support workers, participants, families and internal departments to ensure shifts are filled appropriately, participant needs are met, and staffing arrangements remain compliant and sustainable. 

This is a fast-paced role suited to someone who enjoys problem-solving, communicating clearly, working under pressure, and supporting both staff and participants with professionalism and care. 

Key Responsibilities 

Coordinate and maintain participant and staff rosters in line with participant needs, staff availability and service requirements 

Allocate support workers to shifts, including new engagements, ongoing supports, respite and Supported Independent Living arrangements 

Respond to roster changes, cancellations, unfilled shifts and day-to-day staffing issues in a timely and professional manner 

Communicate clearly with support workers, participants, families, coordinators and internal teams regarding roster updates and changes 

Support smooth handovers for new participants, new staff, first shifts and meet and greets 

Monitor staff availability, shift allocations, travel considerations, skills matching and continuity of support 

Maintain accurate rostering records and documentation within VisualCare and related systems 

Escalate concerns regarding participant safety, staff conduct, availability gaps, compliance risks or service continuity to the Rostering Lead or relevant manager 

Work collaboratively with Recruitment, Clinical, Accounts and Management to support safe and consistent service delivery 

Ensure rostering practices align with Amity Care Services policies, NDIS requirements and SCHADS Award considerations 

About You 

We are looking for someone who is calm, organised and confident communicating with a wide range of people. You will be able to manage competing priorities, think quickly, and remain professional when dealing with last-minute changes or complex rostering issues. 

You will bring: 

Ability to work flexibly across a seven-day roster 

Experience in rostering, scheduling, administration or coordination, ideally within disability, aged care, home care or community services 

Strong communication and interpersonal skills 

Excellent attention to detail and time management 

Ability to work in a busy environment and manage competing priorities 

Confidence using computer systems, Microsoft Office and rostering or care management platforms such as VisualCare 

A practical problem-solving approach and the ability to remain calm under pressure 

A genuine interest in supporting vulnerable people in our community 

Understanding of confidentiality, professional boundaries and respectful communication 

Knowledge of the NDIS, SCHADS Award or community services sector would be highly regarded 

Requirements 

NDIS Worker Screening Check and Working with Children Check, or willingness to obtain 

Completed NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission Worker Orientation Module, or willingness to complete 

Current driver licence and reliable transport may be required depending on business needs 

Ability to work from our Mornington Peninsula office 

Why Join Amity? 

Be part of a values-driven, growing organisation making a genuine difference 

Work within a supportive and collaborative team environment 

Contribute to safe, reliable and person-centred supports for participants 

Opportunity to build your skills in rostering, coordination, NDIS service delivery and compliance 

Join an organisation that values loyalty, trust, honesty and continuous improvement 

How to Apply 

To apply, please submit a cover letter and current resume outlining your relevant experience, your interest in the Rostering Coordinator role, and what you believe you could bring to Amity Care Services to recruitment@amitycareservices.com.au.  

Applications close: 3rd August 2026 

For a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Taryn Brien 1800 426 489.

INVENTORY CONCEPTS
Pymble, Sydney, NSW 2073

Full Time Contract Administrator
SALARY:  $87,500 per annum plus superannuation 

Position 
The Contract Administrator is responsible for the administration, performance monitoring, and commercial management of all client contracts and fixed-rate service agreements across the business. The role plays a critical part in ensuring contractual compliance, maintaining profitability, protecting contract margins and compliance, and delivering operational efficiencies throughout the supply chain and logistics network. 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Contract Administration and Commercial Management 
•	Administer and manage all client contracts and fixed-price service agreements to ensure compliance with contractual obligations and service level requirements. 
•	Monitor contract performance, profitability, and operational outcomes against agreed contractual terms. 
•	Develop, review, negotiate, and implement contract variations, renewals, extensions, and service agreements. 
•	Identify and implement initiatives to improve contract profitability and operational efficiency. 
•	Maintain accurate contract documentation, pricing schedules, and commercial records. 
Financial Analysis and Business Improvement 
•	Analyse operational, financial, and performance data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for cost reduction and productivity improvements. 
•	Develop pricing models and costing structures for existing and prospective contracts. 
•	Prepare costing and pricing inputs for contract renewals, variations and client quotation responses. 
•	Conduct commercial analysis of contract performance to support contract negotiations, variations and renewals. 
•	Prepare forecasting data and performance reports to support future business planning. 
Client and Stakeholder Management 
•	Build and maintain strong relationships with existing and prospective clients. 
•	Act as a key point of contact for contractual matters and service-related issues. 
•	Ensure client expectations and contractual deliverables are clearly understood and consistently achieved. 
•	Support client retention initiatives and identify opportunities to expand service offerings within existing contracts. 
•	Participate in contract review meetings with clients, subcontractors and management. 
Supply Chain and Operational Coordination 
•	Work closely with logistics, warehouse, and inventory management teams to ensure contractual requirements are effectively delivered. 
•	Coordinate subcontractor performance to ensure service delivery standards, compliance requirements, and commercial objectives are achieved. 
•	Monitor operational performance against contractual KPIs and agreed service levels. 
•	Assist in the implementation of continuous improvement initiatives across supply chain operations.
Contract Compliance, Risk and Reporting 
•	Analyse risks associated with specific contract terms and advise management on appropriate mitigation. 
•	Monitor relevant legislative, award and regulatory changes affecting contracts and coordinate with management and external advisers as required. 
•	Interpret and explain contract requirements, terms and conditions to internal stakeholders, clients and subcontractors to support compliance. 
•	Maintain and improve contract-management systems and records, including the in-house platform, to support accurate and efficient contract administration. 
•	Assist in the preparation and negotiation of contract terms, renewals and variations with clients and subcontractors. 

SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, AND EXPERIENCE 
•	Demonstrated experience in contract administration, commercial management, or supply chain contract management. 
•	Strong financial and commercial acumen with the ability to analyse costs, profitability, and operational performance. 
•	Experience within logistics, warehousing, inventory management, third-party logistics (3PL), or supply chain environments. 
•	Sound understanding of fixed-price service agreements, contract compliance, and service level management. 
•	Proven ability to manage multiple stakeholders and maintain strong client relationships. 
•	Experience in pricing analysis, contract negotiation, and the administration of contract variations and renewals. 
•	Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with advanced data interpretation capabilities. 
•	Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
•	High-level computer literacy and proficiency in business systems, reporting tools, and data analysis software. 
•	Knowledge of warehouse operations, distribution centres, inventory control, container handling, and material handling equipment (MHE). 
•	Demonstrated understanding of Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) requirements within 
•	logistics and distribution environments. 
•	Relevant qualifications in Business, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Operations 
•	Management, Information Technology, or a related discipline at AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma level or above. 
•	A demonstrable track record in WHS and its applications in fast paced and dynamic distribution facilities. 


Applications open on 24 July 2026 and close on 23 August 2026
Please send your CV to info@businessnest.com.au. Please include the job role title in your email.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 







We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 







As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 







Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network.



Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.





To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.


Help shape the future of healthcare at Monash Health and embark on a rewarding career where your dedication makes a difference in people's lives.



About the Role



Join our team as an Environmental Services Assistant on a part time ongoing to work at The Victorian Heart Hospital, based in Clayton. In this role, you will be guided under the leadership of the General Services Manager, and working with the broader Support Services team.



ESAs are responsible for maintaining a clean, hygienic, and safe hospital environment; not only for patients, but also for visitors and colleagues across Monash Health. ESAs deliver high-quality environmental services across clinical and non-clinical areas.



Key responsibilities include, but not limited to:




Ensuring adherence to infection prevention and control protocols at all times


Adhering to safety protocols when using cleaning chemicals and equipment in line with safety guidelines


Managing waste removal and disposal procedures safely and responsibly


Maintaining cleaning schedules and documentation


Reporting maintenance or safety hazards promptly


Collaborating with clinical and support teams to deliver service excellence


Completing relevant workplace training modules 


Distribution and collection of linen


Physical work including lifting and manual handling




We currently have the following opportunities available:



Position 1:


Days: Saturday-Tuesday


Hours: 6.30-15.00 (8hrs)


Total hours per fortnight: 64





Position 2:


Days: Tuesday - Wednesday


Hours: 1430-2300 (8hrs)


Total hours per fortnight: 32



Position 3:


Days: Monday - Thursday


Hours: 2230-0700 (8hrs)


Total hours per fortnight: 64



Position 4:


Days: Thursday


Hours: 6.30-15.00 (8hrs)


Total hours per fortnight: 16



 Position 5 


 Days: Saturday & Sunday 


 Hours :06:30- 15:00 (8hrs)


 Total hours Per fortnight: 32 



About You



To ensure your success in this role, you will bring experience in environmental services within a hospital, Aged Care or commercial cleaning setting with strong demonstrated knowledge of infection control and hygiene practices. You are a reliable and punctual team member with great verbal and written communication skills. Whether you're work independently or as part of a team; you always follow manual handling, safety protocols, and procedural instructions.



Why you will love working with us



As an ESA, you will play a vital role in supporting patient care while working within a supportive and inclusive team culture. Monash Health offers ongoing opportunities for professional development and leadership training. ESAs benefit from job stability within Victoria's largest public health service, along with clear career pathways across environmental and support services.



As a Monash Health employee you will enjoy a variety of benefits, such as:




Salary packaging options to increase your take-home pay


Novated leasing for vehicle options


Full-time employees accrue 5 week's annual leave (pro rata for part-time employees) 


Free annual flu vaccinations


Uniform and laundry allowance




About the Department - Program



The Support Services team is a collaborative and dedicated group that plays a crucial role in maintaining a safe, clean, and welcoming environment for patients, visitors, and staff. Our culture is built on respect, compassion, and excellence, and we are committed to continuous improvement and professional development.


 About Victorian Heart Hospital:


Australia's first dedicated cardiac hospital, located in Clayton at Monash University's Clayton campus. It offers world-class cardiovascular care, research, and education, with advanced facilities for cardiac procedures, imaging, and specialist treatment.




For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Amanda Deprinse 0488 387 021. 



Position Description can be found here




Our Culture and Values 







At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 







Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 







You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 







We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 







We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 





How to Apply



Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. For information including how to apply and probity check requirements, please click here for the 'Application Guide'



Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date. 


Applications close: 13 July 2026.    Click here to Apply now →

Diesel Motor Mechanic
Coath Rd, West Kalgoorlie WA 6430
Ful-time

Our client, VPT Mechanical Solutions, is seeking experienced Diesel Motor Mechanics to join their growing team in West Kalgoorlie, Western Australia. As part of the VPT Group, a leading Western Australian industrial services company supporting mining and resource operations, they deliver mechanical, fire suppression, and drilling support services with a strong focus on safety, reliability, quality, and operational excellence.

This is an excellent opportunity for qualified Diesel Motor Mechanics who are looking to build a long-term career within a supportive and professional environment.

Key Responsibilities

* Diagnose and rectify mechanical and electrical faults in diesel engines, heavy vehicles, and mobile equipment.
* Dismantle, inspect, repair, and reassemble engines, transmissions, steering systems, suspension, braking systems, and other mechanical components.
* Replace worn or defective parts in accordance with manufacturer specifications and service manuals.
* Perform routine servicing and preventative maintenance, including oil changes, lubrication, engine tune-ups, and scheduled inspections.
* Test and adjust repaired components to ensure safe and efficient operation.
* Use computer-based diagnostic equipment to identify faults and assess engine performance.
* Inspect vehicles and equipment for roadworthiness and compliance, recommending repairs where required.
* Attend breakdowns and provide on-site mechanical support when necessary.
* Maintain accurate service records while adhering to workplace health and safety procedures.

Skills and Qualifications

* Relevant trade qualification in Diesel Mechanics or an equivalent automotive mechanical trade.
* **Minimum of three (3) years of relevant full-time experience** as a Diesel Motor Mechanic.
* Strong diagnostic, troubleshooting, and problem-solving abilities.
* Experience working with diesel engines, heavy vehicles, and mining or industrial equipment is highly regarded.
* Sound understanding of workplace health and safety requirements.
* Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team.
* Relevant licences and certifications will be advantageous.

What Our Client Offers

* Competitive annual salary of AUD $90,000 – $100,000, depending on qualifications and experience.
* Full-time, long-term employment opportunity.
* Supportive and safety-focused workplace culture.
* Ongoing training and career development opportunities.
* Opportunity to work with a respected Western Australian industrial services company supporting the mining and resources sector.

Part-Time Sewing & Customer Service Assistant ????

Love sewing? Passionate about fashion? Looking for a role where your skills really matter?

We’re looking for a talented and enthusiastic person to join our busy alterations studio. If you enjoy working with garments, appreciate quality craftsmanship, and love helping customers, we’d love to hear from you.

About the Role

This is a hands-on position combining garment alterations with customer service. You’ll work on a wide variety of clothing and be part of a small, supportive team that takes pride in delivering beautiful results.

Sewing Experience Required

We’re looking for someone who has experience using industrial sewing machines and is confident working with different fabrics and garments.

Ideally, you have experience with:
	•	Clothing alterations and repairs.
	•	Taking up hems on dresses, skirts, trousers, and jeans.
	•	Replacing zippers and repairing seams.
	•	Adjusting garment fit, including sleeves, waists, and side seams.
	•	Working with delicate fabrics as well as denim and heavier materials.
	•	Reading garments carefully and finding practical sewing solutions.
	•	Producing neat, high-quality workmanship with excellent attention to detail.

Customer Service

You’ll also:
	•	Welcome customers and assist with fittings.
	•	Take alteration orders and accurately record customer requirements.
	•	Answer enquiries in a friendly and professional manner.
	•	Ensure every customer has a positive experience from drop-off to collection.

We’d Love to Meet You If You
	•	Have previous garment alteration or sewing experience.
	•	Are confident operating industrial sewing machines.
	•	Have customer service experience.
	•	Love fashion and quality craftsmanship.
	•	Are reliable, organised, and take pride in your work.
	•	Enjoy working in a small team and are willing to continue learning.

Why Join Us?

? Flexible part-time hours.

? Friendly and supportive workplace.

? Work on a wide variety of garments every day.

? An opportunity to develop your sewing skills and be part of a business that values quality and craftsmanship.

If sewing is more than just a job for you, and you enjoy creating garments that fit beautifully, we’d love to hear from you.

Please send us your resume to 9stitchesnorthcote@gmail.com and a short introduction telling us about your sewing experience and why you’d like to join our team.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Lead transformative mental health service improvement initiatives

Drive patient flow, quality care and system-wide performance

Join NSW's largest mental health service at Cumberland Hospital

Lead change, build capability and drive innovative mental health solutions that improve patient outcomes, patient flow and service performance.

Employment Type: Permanent Full Time 
Position Classification: Nurse Manager Grade 3 
Remuneration: $153,629.36 - $156,478.31 per annum
Hours Per Week: 38
Located in: Cumberland Hospital

What you'll be doing 
As the Whole of Health Nurse Manager - Mental Health Services, you will lead and support clinicians and service managers to deliver strategic projects that improve patient flow, service efficiency and clinical outcomes. Using Clinical Redesign methodologies, you'll drive sustainable change across Mental Health Services while supporting achievement of key performance targets, including Emergency Treatment Performance (ETP).

You will champion innovative approaches to care delivery and build capability across teams to embed improvements into everyday practice.

Lead service improvement and redesign projects that enhance patient flow and access to care

Coach and support managers and clinicians to achieve measurable performance outcomes

Identify and implement innovative models of care that improve patient experiences and outcomes

Drive sustainable process improvements that strengthen clinical safety, quality and resource utilisation

Partner with consumers, clinicians and stakeholders to deliver person-centred and high-quality services

Join Us

Become part of a team that's transforming mental health care across Western Sydney. If you're passionate about leading change, empowering others and delivering better outcomes for consumers, we encourage you to apply. Apply now and help shape healthier futures through collaboration, innovation and exceptional care at Western Sydney Local Health District.

How to Apply 
Apply online by submitting your resume and addressing the criteria listed below by providing examples that demonstrate your ability before the closing date.

Essential Requirements:

Qualification: Registered Nurse with relevant tertiary qualifications 
Registration: Currently held AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse 

Selection Criteria:

Relevant Tertiary Qualifications in Nursing, current registration with AHPRA as RN and demonstrated experience clinical and service improvement experience.

Demonstrated experience in applying project management knowledge to effectively lead and undertake complex projects - and understanding of change management, ideally within a NSW Heath or similar agencies in other jurisdictions.

Demonstrated program, personnel management skills and experience including project design, implementation, reporting and evaluation to ensure high quality deliverables.

Demonstrated experience in analytical skills including the ability to access, assess and critically evaluate project related data and prepare reports and briefs for escalation or stakeholder review.

Demonstrated high level interpersonal, negotiation and communication skills with the ability to prepare and facilitate presentations for executive, stakeholders and large groups with the ability to work within a multidisciplinary team, lead others to foster innovation, achieve outcomes, meet deadlines and achieve project objectives.

Well-developed oral and written communication skills, including the ability to prepare high level reports and papers for publication, as well as sound negotiation and interpersonal skills

Demonstrated ability to inspire, lead and motivate staff and stakeholders, as well as ability to form effective working relationships with senior clinicians, senior manager and external partners.
